findings.title: CARRIED (deferral accepted, my round-1 rule was wrong): invisible/bidi characters still survive sanitizeGroupTitle — corrected, ZWJ-safe rule handed to Task 8
findings.description:
Answering the explicit challenge: I do NOT think this must land in Task 03, and I am withdrawing the regex I proposed in round 1 because it was defective. My round-1 recommendation was `/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F\u200B-\u200F\u202A-\u202E\u2066-\u2069\uFEFF]/g`. The range `\u200B-\u200F` contains U+200C ZWNJ and U+200D ZWJ, so that rule would have flattened `\uD83D\uDC68\u200D\uD83D\uDC69\u200D\uD83D\uDC67` (family emoji) into three separate glyphs and would have damaged legitimate Persian/Indic orthography. The task's objection (a) lands, even though it is framed against a 'blanket Cf strip' that I did not propose — the specific rule I wrote had the ZWJ bug in it. Objection (b) is the stronger one and I accept it as sequencing: Decision 7 makes the loader and `updateBoard` a matched pair, so a rule that lives in only one of them changes a stored title on reload. Deferring to Task 8, where both sites can land it in one step, is the correct call and matches CLAUDE.md's scope discipline.

What remains factually true and unrepaired in the current build (re-verified against src/data/migration.ts:38-46 at 8d76086): `trim()` strips WhiteSpace + LineTerminator only, so `sanitizeGroupTitle('\u200B')` returns a length-1 non-empty string, `sanitizeGroupTitle('\u202Etfarcni')` is preserved verbatim, and embedded `\n`/`\t`/`\u0000` survive. Because `''` is the sentinel for 'use the localized default' (types.ts:29), an all-invisible title suppresses the default name and renders a blank header, and loadPluginData() (src/main.ts:52-59) writes that state straight back to disk. Not XSS — the value reaches the DOM only through Svelte `{}` interpolation, and the repo-wide `{@html}` ban still holds (grep over src/ finds it only inside a comment in src/ui/groupTitle.ts). Also still open from round 1: 40 stacked combining marks pass the cap as a legal 40-character title and render far taller than one header row; that half is a CSS concern (`overflow: hidden` on the header), not a sanitizer concern.
findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:38-46 (sanitizeGroupTitle) — fix belongs in Task 8, applied to both this function and updateBoard
findings.impact: Unchanged from round 1: a damaged or hand-crafted data.json can produce a group with no readable name, or a header whose visible text reads as another group's. Sticky across restarts because the sanitized value is persisted on load. Display integrity only; no code execution, no privilege consequence.

findings.title: NEW: the surrogate strip makes the loader's normalization differ from the one Task 8 is specified to write, breaking the Decision 7 'same rule in both places' symmetry
findings.description:
This is a direct consequence of the round-1 fix, and it is worth naming now because Task 8 has not been written yet. Task 8 §Decision 10 (docs/.../task-08.md:88-92) specifies `updateBoard` as 'trim each incoming name and cap it at 40 characters', and its acceptance test asserts a 60-character title is stored with length 40 — i.e. plain `trim().slice(0, 40)`. `sanitizeGroupTitle` is now `trim().slice(0, 40).replace(/[\uD800-\uDBFF]$/, '')`. The two sites are no longer the same operation. Any value that ends on a lone high surrogate after `updateBoard` runs would be silently shortened by one code unit on the next plugin load — exactly the 'title changes under the user's feet on reload' failure mode that was used to justify deferring the invisible-character rule.

Reachability today is effectively nil, and I want to be precise about why rather than overstate this: HTML `maxlength` is defined on the code-unit length of the value, browsers reject an insertion that would exceed it rather than splitting it, and no code path feeds `updateBoard` programmatically. So the UI cannot produce a 41-code-unit value, `updateBoard`'s cap never fires on a surrogate boundary, and the divergence cannot be observed. It becomes observable the moment a second entry point appears (import, sync merge, a settings paste path that sets `.value` directly) or the cap changes.
findings.impact: None observable in the current build. The cost is a documented invariant (Decision 7: loader and store boundary normalize identically) that is now false in the code, which is precisely the kind of drift that makes the next reader trust the wrong site.

findings.category: A08: Software and Data Integrity Failures
findings.title: CARRIED (deferral accepted): sanitization ignores the stored version, so a file written by a newer plugin version is silently downgraded and rewritten
findings.description: Unchanged by 8d76086 — the sanitization block (src/data/migration.ts:151-159) still sits outside every `if (version < N)` branch in the forward direction as well as the backward one. For `version > 8` all migration branches are skipped and the sanitizers still run: sanitizeGroupOrder drops every id not in the currently compiled GROUP_IDS and appends the six it knows, and sanitizeGroupTitle truncates at the currently compiled 40. loadPluginData() then persists the result with `await this.saveData(this.data)` (src/main.ts:52-59) before anything renders, with no backup and no user-facing message (Decision 6). The realistic trigger is a vault synced across two machines on different plugin versions — the normal state of an Obsidian vault on Sync/Dropbox/git — not a deliberate downgrade. I agree with recording rather than fixing: Decision 10 rules out a CURRENT_VERSION constant and the blast radius is zero while GROUP_IDS is fixed at six and the cap at 40.
findings.impact: Permanent, silent loss of user configuration the first time the group set or the title cap changes and a vault is opened by an older build. Zero today.
findings.recommendation: Keep as recorded. When schema 9 lands, make migrateData return the data untouched when it sees a version it does not understand, so an unknown-future file is never rewritten — that is strictly better than gating the sanitizers on `version <= 8`, because it also protects fields this build has never heard of. Worth a line in the tech-spec's Backward Compatibility section, which currently reasons only about older data. Verification note: the Task 03 section of the decisions log does not exist yet (the file has sections for Tasks 01, 02 and 05 only), so this finding's agreed mitigation — the written record — is still outstanding.

findings.title: CARRIED (no-guard decision accepted, re-verified): the sanitization block can still throw on malformed board/groups shapes, and the new test's title reads as a stronger guarantee than it gives
findings.description:
Re-checked against the committed code and against the two new tests. The block still throws TypeError when `board` is null, when `board.groups` is missing/null/primitive (`Object.values(undefined)`), or when an own value of `board.groups` is null or a primitive (strict mode, so `(42).title = ''` throws). I re-confirmed the mitigating analysis that made this minor rather than major: cleanupCompletedTasks (`board.groups.completed.completedRetentionDays`, src/data/cleanup.ts:4) and cleanupOrphanedTasks (src/data/cleanup.ts:22-26) run immediately afterwards in the same function and throw on every one of these same shapes, so the block moves the failure earlier rather than creating a new class of unloadable file. Not adding guards is the right call under the task's explicit prohibition.

One observation on the new coverage, which is otherwise a genuine improvement: the test named 'a board missing a group does not throw and is still repaired' (tests/unit/migration.test.ts) is accurate about migrateData but the board it produces is not usable. It deletes `groups.orgIntentions`, and BoardLayout.svelte:25-27 maps a fixed six-id list through `board.groups[id].fullWidth`, so that board throws at first render. The choice of `orgIntentions` is also what keeps the test green through cleanup.ts — deleting `completed` instead would throw at cleanup.ts:4. Both facts predate this task; the risk is only that the test name invites a future reader to conclude migrateData plus the loader are total over a board with a missing group.
findings.location: src/data/migration.ts:151-159; tests/unit/migration.test.ts (test 'a board missing a group does not throw and is still repaired')
findings.impact: None beyond the status quo. The concern is documentation drift: the file-level comment (src/data/migration.ts:9-10) and now a test name both read as guarantees about migrateData that only hold for the two sanitizer functions.
findings.recommendation: Cheapest close: rename the test to what it actually asserts — e.g. 'a board missing a group does not throw in migrateData' — and, if the decisions log entry for Task 03 is written, note there that migrateData surviving such a board does not make it renderable (BoardLayout.svelte:27) or cleanable (cleanup.ts:4). No code change. Also relevant to Tasks 06/07: sanitizeGroupOrder always returns all six ids, so a groupOrder-driven render loop will index a group that may not exist — the same crash surface as today's hardcoded literal, not a worse one, but do not assume groupOrder implies the group object is present.

findings.title: CARRIED (accepted): sanitizeGroupOrder scans the whole stored array with no early exit or input bound
findings.description: Unchanged (src/data/migration.ts:23-28). The loop walks every element of the stored array although the result can never hold more than six ids and `seen` is full after at most six accepted items. Cost is O(n) with a six-element `includes` scan per item, on the main thread, inside onload, on every load. I accept the disposition without reservation: the six-element domain makes the extra branch a net readability cost, the output is correctly bounded so nothing accumulates on disk, and the amplification over the JSON.parse Obsidian already performed on the same bytes is negligible. Recording it is the right weight for it.
findings.impact: A pathologically large stored groupOrder delays plugin load proportionally to its length, bounded by what JSON.parse already survived. Slow start, not a hang.
findings.recommendation: No action. If it is ever revisited, `if (seen.size === GROUP_IDS.length) break;` at the end of the loop body is the whole fix and no existing test changes.

findings.title: CARRIED (accepted): unknown keys inside board.groups are neither validated nor pruned — no prototype pollution, re-verified
findings.description: Unchanged and still clean on the part that matters. The order path gates every stored value through `GROUP_IDS.includes(id)` (src/data/migration.ts:25), SameValueZero with no coercion, so `'__proto__'`, `'constructor'` and `'prototype'` are dropped and never reach a property write. The title path uses `Object.values(board.groups)`, which reads own enumerable values and never uses a stored key as an assignment target, so no attacker-controlled string is ever a write destination. `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"x":1}}')` does materialise `__proto__` as an own enumerable data property, so such an entry is visited — but the write lands on that plain object's own `title` and `Object.getPrototypeOf` is untouched. Residual, as before: junk keys under `board.groups` get a `title` written and are carried through migrateData into saveData (src/main.ts:59) load after load, and cleanupOrphanedTasks (src/data/cleanup.ts:23) treats them as real groups, so task ids parked under an unknown key keep those tasks alive. Agreeing that pruning is a data-destroying operation that needs its own decision.
findings.impact: No prototype pollution and no privilege consequence. Junk group entries persist indefinitely in data.json and keep orphaned tasks reachable.
findings.recommendation: No action for this task. Record the asymmetry (groupOrder drops unknown ids, groups keeps unknown keys) so the two fields' differing definitions of 'a group that exists' are a decision rather than an accident. If it is ever addressed: iterate GROUP_IDS for the write while keeping Object.values for the read, and delete unknown keys only behind an explicit versioned migration step.

findings.title: NEW (pre-existing, surfaced by the refactor): freshDefaultData() returns an object whose settings, tasks and boards[0].groups are still the live DEFAULT_DATA instances — only groupOrder is copied
findings.description:
Not introduced by 8d76086 — the extracted function is byte-identical in behaviour to the two literals it replaces, which I saw and did not flag in round 1. Raising it now because the extraction gives the aliasing a name and a comment, and the comment reasons about exactly this hazard while covering only one of the four aliased fields. `freshDefaultData()` (src/data/migration.ts:51-56) does `{ ...DEFAULT_DATA, boards: [{ ...DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0], groupOrder: [...] }] }`. A shallow spread copies references: the returned `settings` object, the returned `tasks` dictionary, and the returned `boards[0].groups` record (with all six mutable group objects inside it) are the same instances DEFAULT_DATA owns — a module-level singleton built once by `createDefaultBoard('My Project')` (src/data/defaults.ts:53-58). `src/main.ts:14` and `src/stores/dataStore.ts:11` alias the same three objects the same way.

Runtime impact today is nil, which is why this is minor and not more: nothing in src/ reads DEFAULT_DATA expecting pristine values after load (createDefaultBoard builds fresh groups from DEFAULT_FULL_WIDTH and does not touch DEFAULT_DATA), and Obsidian re-evaluates the bundle on disable/enable, so the singleton does not survive a plugin reload. The concrete cost is test isolation: in a vitest file the module registry is shared across tests, so any test that calls `migrateData(null)` or `migrateData({version: 0})` and then mutates a group title or pushes a taskId permanently mutates DEFAULT_DATA for every later test in that file. tests/unit/migration.test.ts:292-304 already asserts DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0].groupOrder is intact, so this hazard was anticipated for the one field that was fixed.
findings.impact: No user-visible consequence in the current build. A silent test-pollution channel, and a comment that documents aliasing awareness while three of the four aliased fields are still shared — the shape that produces a wrong assumption in the next change.
